key_insight: Random, intermittent jet forcing can both mix and sharpen a salt-stratified fluid interface, with interface rise slowing as the density jump increases.
engineering_relevance: The results help predict how stratified interfaces evolve under unsteady turbulent forcing in environmental and industrial flows where transport and mixing control performance.
method: Two-layer salt-stratified fluid was forced by a randomly actuated synthetic jet array (RASJA).
Interface density evolution was measured using light attenuation imaging.
Background potential energy was used to assess irreversible mixing.
evidence_signal: Experiments showed that interface upward velocity decreases with density jump, and at large density differences the interface sharpened during mixing while still exhibiting comparable irreversible energy changes.
watch_item: The findings come from laboratory-scale, two-layer stratified conditions, so direct transfer to complex natural flows may require caution.
paper_title: Mixing and sharpening at the interface of a two-layer fluid forced by random jets
